svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: Three-tier web application on AWS subtitle: Load-balanced EC2 web tier across two Availability Zones, Aurora and ElastiCache in private subnets direction: down # merge: false gives each edge its own port: the two NAT paths would otherwise share one arrowhead # at the internet gateway. layout: { merge: false } legend: solid: Application traffic dashed: Outbound via NAT groups: cloud: { type: aws:cloud } region: { type: aws:region, label: us-east-1, in: cloud } vpc: { type: aws:vpc, label: VPC 10.0.0.0/16, in: region } az-a: { type: aws:az, label: Availability Zone A, in: vpc } az-b: { type: aws:az, label: Availability Zone B, in: vpc } public-a: { type: aws:public-subnet, label: Public subnet, in: az-a } public-b: { type: aws:public-subnet, label: Public subnet, in: az-b } # The web and data tiers each get a private subnet per zone; the nodes say which tier is which. app-a: { type: aws:private-subnet, label: Private subnet, in: az-a } app-b: { type: aws:private-subnet, label: Private subnet, in: az-b } data-a: { type: aws:private-subnet, label: Private subnet, in: az-a } data-b: { type: aws:private-subnet, label: Private subnet, in: az-b } # One Auto Scaling group spans both zones: an overlay that does not move its members. asg: { type: aws:auto-scaling, around: [app-a, app-b] } nodes: users: { icon: aws:users, label: Users } igw: { icon: aws:igw, label: Internet gateway, in: vpc } alb: { icon: aws:alb, label: Application Load Balancer, note: Public subnets in both AZs, in: vpc } nat-a: { icon: aws:nat, label: NAT gateway, in: public-a } nat-b: { icon: aws:nat, label: NAT gateway, in: public-b } web-a: { icon: aws:ec2-instance, label: Web server, note: Amazon EC2 instance, in: app-a } web-b: { icon: aws:ec2-instance, label: Web server, note: Amazon EC2 instance, in: app-b } db-a: { icon: aws:aurora-instance, label: Amazon Aurora, note: Primary (writer), in: data-a } db-b: { icon: aws:aurora-instance, label: Amazon Aurora, note: Replica (reader), in: data-b } cache-a: { icon: aws:elasticache-cache-node, label: Amazon ElastiCache, note: Primary node, in: data-a } cache-b: { icon: aws:elasticache-cache-node, label: Amazon ElastiCache, note: Replica node, in: data-b } edges: - users -> igw: HTTPS - igw -> alb - alb -> web-a, web-b: HTTP # Outbound traffic goes up through the NAT gateways; written in layout order (NAT first) # with the arrow at the start, so the public subnets stay above the private ones. - { from: igw, to: [nat-a, nat-b], arrow: start, line: dashed } - { from: nat-a, to: web-a, arrow: start, line: dashed } - { from: nat-b, to: web-b, arrow: start, line: dashed } # One arrow into each data subnet stands for the database and the cache. - web-a -> data-a: reads and writes - web-b -> data-b: reads # Zone B writes go to the primary Aurora and ElastiCache nodes in zone A. constraint: false keeps # this edge out of the layout, so the zones stay side by side. - { from: web-b, to: data-a, label: writes, constraint: false }

svg.title: Three-tier web application on AWS
svg.desc: Three-tier web application on AWS. 11 components in 12 groups. Connections: Users to Internet gateway (HTTPS); Internet gateway to Application Load Balancer; Application Load Balancer to Web server (HTTP); Application Load Balancer to Web server (HTTP); Internet gateway to NAT gateway; Internet gateway to NAT gateway; NAT gateway to Web server; NAT gateway to Web server; Web server to Private subnet (reads and writes); Web server to Private subnet (reads); Web server to Private subnet (writes).

text.tspan: Load-balanced EC2 web tier across two Availability Zones, Aurora and ElastiCache in private subnets
